blacklistabilityReview.sourceFreeRationale: The current holder-facing CADm token has no direct governance-controlled blacklist, freeze, pause, seizure, arbitrary-account burn, or transfer-hook restriction. Broker/exchange burn and Celo-VM gas debiting are protocol-scoped, not governance holder-freeze controls. Timelocked proxy upgrade authority is recorded in mint-authority evidence but is not itself a currently executable holder-freeze surface. This direct conclusion does not suppress reserve-derived upstream exposure.
blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Re-verified 2026-08-08 at Celo block 74317848. CADm 0xff4ab19391af240c311c54200a492233052b6325 still returned Mento Timelock 0x890db8a597940165901372dd7db61c9f246e2147 as owner, Broker 0x777a8255ca72412f0d706dc03c9d1987306b4cad, validators 0xaeb865bca93ddc8f47b8e29f40c5399ce34d0c58, and a zero exchange; its implementation remained verified StableTokenV2 0x434563b0604be100f04b7ae485bcafe3c9d8850e. Verified transfer paths have no blacklist, freeze, pause, seizure, arbitrary-holder burn, allowlist, or governance transfer hook. Broker/exchange burn is caller-scoped and debitGasFees is Celo-VM scoped. Mento governance can replace implementation only through the observed 172800-second timelock, so current direct blacklistability is false while deployment posture remains restrictable. USDC, USDT, EURC, and related shared-reserve exposures can impair backing but cannot restrict CADm balances and are therefore dependency risk, not an inherited direct-access verdict.
